newsitem.title: USA: USDA lowers FY97 ag export forecast to $55.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: USDA lowers FY97 ag export forecast to $55.5 bln.

text.p: The Agriculture Department Wednesday lowered it fiscal 1997 forecast for U.S. agricultural exports to $55.5 bln, $2.5 bln lower than projected in August, and $4.3 bln less than 1996.
Sharp declines in expected prices for wheat, coarse grains, and soybeans account for most of the reduction, USDA said.
Increased foreign production and higher competitor exports of wheat and coarse grains has resulted in reduced prospects for U.S. shipments since August.
USDA estimated the volume of agricultural exports in FY97 at 146.7 million tonnes, down from its previous estimate of 150.5 million and below last year's 158.4 million tonnes.
Major bulk exports are forecast at 104.9 million tonnes, 14 million less than in FY96.
The FY97 export projection is still the third highest on record, said USDA economist Joel Greene, on USDA radio.
High-value product exports are expected to rise by almost $2 bln to a record $33 bln and will account for nearly 60 percent of U.S. agricultural exports.

Prospects for livestock producers have also declined since August, but exports of these commodities are still forecast at a record $8.7 billion. Record poultry meat and horticulture exports are also expected.
U.S. agricultural imports in FY97 are forecast at a record $34 bln, up $2 bln from the August projection.
Animal and horticultural products are expected to provide the boost to imports in 1997.
The FY97 agricultural trade surplus is projected at $21.5 bln, down $4.5 bln from the August projection, and $5.9 bln less than the record $27.4 billion surplus in 1996.
